newsitem.title: CHINA: Chna should delist loss-making firms - paper.
newsitem.headline: Chna should delist loss-making firms - paper.

text.p: The official Shenzhen-based Securities Times newspaper on Friday called on Chinese securities authorities to delist public companies incurring losses for three straight years.
"According to Company Law, securities regulators must delist listed firms that make losses for three consecutive years," the newspaper said in a commentary.
Seven companies listed in Shenzhen or Shanghai had reported losses for the past two years, and their losses were expanding, it said.

All seven companies were domestic A share firms, including the Shanghai-listed Huanghe Machinery and Electronics Co, a refrigerator and television maker, and Shekou Anda Industry Co, a land transportation company.
Regulators should implement the law to protect investor interests, the newspaper said.
In the seven-year history of modern China's stock market, no companies have so far been delisted.
